_note: Replaces the targets.csv named in README.md — the data is too nested for CSV. Every value here was retrieved from ChEMBL, RCSB, UniProt or a cited publication. Nothing is recalled or estimated. Values that could not be retrieved are the string NOT_FOUND.
_expected_output: What a correct dossier must say. This is the grading key for the fixture run.

_measurement_definitions._why: A grading key with no stated definition drifts. Every count below was re-measured 2026-08-15 against Paperclip (sql -s proteins) with the definitions in this block. If you change a definition, re-measure the whole file — do not patch one number.
_measurement_definitions.distinct_compounds: COUNT(DISTINCT molregno) FROM chembl_v.bioactivities_by_accession WHERE accession=<ACC> AND n_target_components = 1. The n_target_components=1 predicate is LOAD-BEARING and is the single most common way to get these numbers wrong — see _audit_2026_08_15.
_measurement_definitions.total_activities: COUNT(*) over the same view with the same n_target_components = 1 predicate.
_measurement_definitions.best_potency_nm: MAX(pchembl_value) over the same filtered set, converted 10^(9-pchembl), AND THEN rejected if the source assay description is uncharacterised per CLAUDE.md rule 6 ('Inhibition of X (unknown origin)', 'Binding affinity to X (unknown origin)'). Where the raw maximum is rejected on that ground the entry says so explicitly. standard_relation must be '='.
_measurement_definitions.pdb_total: COUNT(DISTINCT entry_id) FROM pdb_v.structures_by_accession WHERE accession=<ACC>. NOTE: this view has one row per (accession, entry, entity), so COUNT(*) overcounts — KRAS is 534 rows for 522 entries.
_measurement_definitions._STRUCTURE_AXIS_REGENERATED_2026_08_15: Every pdb_holo / pdb_apo / pdb_undetermined figure below was REGENERATED WHOLESALE on 2026-08-15 under the definition in `pdb_holo`. Nothing was patched. The prior values were produced by the superseded '250-1200 Da + $EXCL' MW-window rule, and before that by '>=300 Da'. Both are gone. Where a regenerated count disagrees with an earlier adjudication, the disagreement is recorded ON THE TARGET rather than reconciled away — see `_structure_regeneration_2026_08_15`.
_measurement_definitions.pdb_holo: CHEMISTRY CLASSIFIER, not a molecular-weight window. An entry is HOLO iff at least one of its components in pdb_v.entry_ligands classifies as `druglike` under `.claude/skills/structure-select/ligand_filter.py::classify_record`. Measured 2026-08-15. Classifier sha256 526610951ee120f95b24731e72b33b2d2901e929626909d775ce6df65289f1f3, 1490 lines, tunables LIPID_MIN_CHAIN=8 / TRIVIAL_MAX_HEAVY_ATOMS=9 / DRUGLIKE_MAX_MW=1200. `classify_record` takes a pdb_v.entry_ligands row verbatim and does NO I/O, so every verdict here is reproducible offline from the row. THERE IS NO LOWER MW BOUND ANY MORE — that is the single biggest behavioural change and it is deliberate: the module's own comment says the old 18-heavy-atom floor 'is gone, because size was never the discriminator', and the floor was demonstrably splitting congeneric series across the holo/apo line.
_measurement_definitions.pdb_apo: an entry with NO `druglike` component AND NO `unknown` component. Strictly narrower than 'not holo'.
_measurement_definitions.pdb_undetermined: an entry with no `druglike` component but at least one component the classifier returned `unknown` for. THIS IS NOT APO AND MUST NEVER BE ADDED TO THE APO COUNT. `unknown` has two causes and both are live in this file: (a) the CCD names the component 'UNKNOWN LIGAND' / unidentified density — TYK2 5C01 carries `UNL`; (b) the component exceeds the 1200 Da ceiling and no cofactor/lipid/peptide signature fired, so the classifier refuses rather than assumes — BCL-2 8FY1 and 8FY2. A third cause, a Paperclip lookup FAILURE, carries the `lookup_failed` flag into holo_call(...)['undetermined'] and is a network fact, not a chemistry fact. pdb_total = pdb_holo + pdb_apo + pdb_undetermined, always.
known_limits_of_the_new_holo_rule: FALSE POSITIVE, measured here and NOT in the classifier's own test set: TNF-alpha 5UUI's MTN (MTSL nitroxide spin label, 264 Da, covalently attached to an engineered T77C cysteine) classifies `druglike`. Its chemistry genuinely is drug-like; what disqualifies it is the entry title ('Crystal Structure of Spin-Labeled T77C TNFa'), which no chemistry test can see. The module's docstring claims 0 false positives on a 70-component held-out sample; that claim is about that sample and MTN was not in it. Chemistry alone cannot catch a covalent biophysical probe.

FALSE NEGATIVE, declared by the module and live here: nucleoside/SAM-analog inhibitors classify `cofactor`. STAT3 5AX3's 5ID (a 7-deazaadenosine, 5-iodotubercidin class) is a real nucleoside-analog inhibitor filed as a cofactor. This is why STAT3 moves 3 -> 2. The bias is deliberate and conservative: a false negative costs one holo structure, a false positive invents one.

The 1200 Da CEILING no longer scores degraders as APO — it scores them `unknown`, which is a real improvement over the superseded rule. BCL-2 8FY1 (YF8, 1640 Da) and 8FY2 (YFH, 1682 Da) are genuine bivalent degrader co-crystals and now land in pdb_undetermined, where they are visible, rather than silently in apo.
drugbank_id is not a druglikeness signal and does not gate anything — MTN carries DB08217. The classifier reads the field but never lets it decide.

The hand-written $EXCL comp_id list is NO LONGER USED for these counts. It is reproduced by the classifier's chemistry without having been shown it, and its two documented leaks (MTN; RORgt 4NIE's DMX = NDSB-256 sulfobetaine) are now handled on chemistry — DMX is caught, MTN is not.
_measurement_definitions.how_to_reproduce_and_the_trap_that_will_: Pull pdb_v.entry_ligands for the accession's entries, call classify_record per distinct comp_id, and count entries. THE TRAP IS NOT CHEMISTRY, IT IS PAGING. Paperclip's documented row cap is 200 but the SERVED cap moves under load: on 2026-08-15 the identical entry-list query returned 200 rows at one moment and EXACTLY 10 at another, with no error and a well-formed table both times. A short page is therefore ambiguous between 'end of results' and 'silently truncated', and OFFSET paging under-counts without ever failing. The first run of this regeneration recorded KRAS as 10 entries against a true 522 and would have written it into this grading key as a measurement. EVERY count in this file was re-taken by paging at whatever page size RECONCILES with an independently issued COUNT aggregate, bracketed by a canary on both pdb_v tables (TNF-alpha = 52 entries; 4OBE apo / 6OIM holo on MOV per structure-select SKILL.md §1). A count that does not reconcile is not recorded.
_measurement_definitions.data_validity_comment_is_NOT_usable_here: chembl_v.bioactivities_by_accession exposes a data_validity_comment column that is NULL for EVERY row, on all 11 accessions in this file, exactly like the already-documented always-NULL `modality` column. The raw chembl.activities table does carry it (345,635 'Outside typical range' rows overall; 91 on JAK1) but the VIEW does not propagate it, and the view is not pre-filtered — JAK1 returns all 48,836 raw activity_ids. Separately, JAK1's 91 flagged raw rows carry NO pchembl_value at all, so flagged rows can never be the top-potency rows. Any fixture note claiming top potencies 'were flagged Outside typical range and excluded' is describing a filter that did nothing.

_audit_2026_08_15.headline: The precedent axis is TRUSTWORTHY and does not need regeneration. The structure axis DOES — every holo count in this file was generated with a superseded rule. ChEMBL drift is not the problem and never was: all 11 compound counts and 6 of 7 activity counts re-measured EXACT.
_audit_2026_08_15.the_challenge_that_failed: JAK1 14,342 was reported as stale against a 'measured' 14,472. The fixture was RIGHT and the challenge was WRONG. 14,472 is the same view with the n_target_components = 1 predicate dropped, which pools inherited hits from multi-component targets (complexes, PPI pairs, PROTAC ternary complexes). Verified by reproducing the fixture value exactly on all eleven accessions with the predicate and the inflated value exactly on all eleven without it. Had this been blessed it would have silently corrupted six of the eleven targets.
_audit_2026_08_15.the_challenge_that_succeeded: TNF 15 -> 17 is a real DEFINITION CHANGE from the '>=300 Da' holo rule to the '250-1200 Da + $EXCL' rule. Both rules were re-run and reproduce 15 and 17 exactly. But the right answer is 16, not 17: of the two added entries, 6OOY (A7M, a real benzimidazole from an already-counted series) belongs and 5UUI (MTN = MTSL nitroxide spin label on an engineered T77C cysteine) does not.
_audit_2026_08_15.the_second_challenge_that_succeeded: JAK1 0.032 -> 0.010 nM is a FIXTURE QUERY DEFECT. The fixture excluded all IC50s as 'flagged Outside typical range'; the view never populates that column, and JAK1's genuinely-flagged raw rows carry no pchembl at all. The 0.010 nM value traces to a 2016 document, so data growth cannot explain it, and it is corroborated by 2 compounds x 2 independent assays with 60 compounds above the old value.

factually_wrong_corrected: IL-11 'ALL 15 from a single assay' -> two assays
EGFR and JAK1 'Outside typical range' notes removed as no-ops

_audit_2026_08_15.known_inconsistency_left_in_place: structure-select SKILL.md §1 asserts TNF-alpha is '17 holo / 35 apo'. That matches the rule as written but includes the 5UUI spin label. The skill was not edited (out of scope for this task) and should be corrected separately — the count is right for the rule and the rule is slightly wrong.

_structure_regeneration_2026_08_15._what: The structure axis was regenerated WHOLESALE under the chemistry classifier. Read `_measurement_definitions.pdb_holo` for the definition and the classifier hash. This block records WHICH targets were re-measured, which were not, and why — because a half-regenerated grading key is worse than a stale one only when nobody can tell which half is which.

measured_and_reconciled._meaning: pdb_holo / pdb_apo / pdb_undetermined below are the classifier's output, taken under a passing canary and reconciled against an independently issued COUNT aggregate.
measured_and_reconciled.MYC P01106: 25 / 0 / 25 / 0 (unchanged at 0, now under a fifth independent rule)
measured_and_reconciled.CD20 P11836 (control, not a fixture targ: 10 / 0 / 10 / 0 — run as a positive control on the classifier's headline case; pentadecane, phosphatidylcholine and cholesterol hemisuccinate all correctly filed lipid_or_detergent. Confirms the adjudicated 'CD20 true holo is 0'.

NOT_regenerated_original_values_left_in_._meaning: Paperclip's sql backend failed before these five could be re-measured. THEIR pdb_holo FIGURES ARE STILL THE OLD MW-WINDOW VALUES and are marked as such on each target. Do not read them as regenerated. Do not average them with the regenerated ones.
NOT_regenerated_original_values_left_in_.what_is_needed: Re-run classify_record over pdb_v.entry_ligands for these five accessions when the backend is healthy, reconciling against COUNT aggregates. The BCL-2 case is the one to watch: under the new rule 8FY1 (YF8, 1640 Da) and 8FY2 (YFH, 1682 Da) should land in pdb_undetermined, NOT apo, because the classifier returns `unknown` above its 1200 Da ceiling rather than assuming — which is strictly better than the superseded rule, and means the answer is very unlikely to be the previously anticipated 40.

backend_failures._why_recorded: Every one of these produced a well-formed, non-empty, entirely wrong result or no result at all. They are recorded because the next person to regenerate this file will hit them and needs to know that the guards are load-bearing, not ceremony.
backend_failures.1_moving_row_cap: Paperclip's documented cap is 200 rows. The SERVED cap moved to EXACTLY 10 under load, with no error and a well-formed table. The first run of this regeneration recorded KRAS as 10 entries against a true 522. Caught only by reconciling against an independent COUNT.
backend_failures.2_statement_timeouts: Queries that returned in 8 ms at one moment timed out at 120 s minutes later. Multi-accession GROUP BYs and the domain-split CTE in structure-select SKILL.md section 3 both timed out; the CTE had to be replaced by fetching raw alignment ranges and doing the overlap arithmetic in Python.
backend_failures.3_the_endpoint_is_shared_and_capped_at_1: Another client on the same box held 15-21 connections for much of this task. `paperclip` handles the limit itself with up to five backoffs, so a SHORT outer timeout is actively harmful — it kills the client mid-backoff and re-launches it. Tried 20 s and throughput got worse; 150 s with few retries got through.
backend_failures.4_tool_level_breakage: Late in the task every `paperclip sql` began returning `vsh: cd: /papers/: Permission denied` in ~17 ms — not a timeout, a broken tool. `paperclip search` was unaffected. This is what stopped the last five targets.
backend_failures.the_rule_that_saved_the_file: A count is recorded ONLY when it reconciles with a separately issued aggregate, under a canary that checks the two pdb_v tables actually being read (TNF-alpha = 52 entries; 4OBE apo / 6OIM holo on MOV). `SELECT 1` passing tells you nothing about pdb_v. Every failure above was caught by that pair; none was caught by an error code.

disagreements_with_the_prior_adjudicatio._read_this: Three previously adjudicated numbers do not survive the new rule. In each case the adjudication was correct FOR THE RULE IT WAS MADE UNDER and is superseded by the change of rule, not overturned on the facts.
disagreements_with_the_prior_adjudicatio.TNF-alpha 16 -> 20: 16 was (250-1200 Da window) minus the MTSL spin label, so it inherits a 250 Da floor the classifier does not have. It excluded 6X81/6X83, which are from the same J. Med. Chem. paper and the same series as three entries it counted. See the target's pdb_holo_why_the_adjudicated_16_does_not_survive.
disagreements_with_the_prior_adjudicatio.JAK1 42 -> 43: 42 was the MW-window value. Re-derived from scratch as instructed, since 40 reproduced under no rule at all.
disagreements_with_the_prior_adjudicatio.STAT3 3 -> 2: The classifier files 5AX3's nucleoside-analog inhibitor as a cofactor — a false negative it declares in its own docstring.
disagreements_with_the_prior_adjudicatio.and_one_that_CONFIRMS: The TYK2 exclusive domain split 28 / 20 / 1 (4OLI) / 3 reproduced exactly from raw alignment ranges. The old inclusive 29/21, which summed to 54 against a real 52, stays rejected.

_expected_output_audit_2026_08_15._why: A 15-target / 67-structure / 134-measurement evaluation demoted fpocket druggability, which is the number several expected_output blocks in this file were implicitly graded on. Every expected_output was re-read against that evaluation. NOTHING IN THE LADDER'S INTENT WAS REWRITTEN — where a rung no longer tests its stated failure mode, the finding and a PROPOSED replacement are recorded here and the rung is left as it stands, for a human to accept or reject.

what_the_evaluation_established.druggability_does_not_separate: target-level AUC 0.720 at D=1.6, bootstrap CI 0.44-0.94 — includes chance. At D=2.4, AUC 0.520. On 37 holo structures with a drug-like ligand PHYSICALLY BOUND and the pocket anchored to it, median score 0.320, and 15 of 37 (41%) score below 0.1.
what_the_evaluation_established.volume_separation_is_SUSPENDED_do_not_us: The volume separation (AUC 1.000, hard <=207 A^3 / druggable >=242 A^3) was WITHDRAWN on 2026-08-15, after this audit block was first drafted and before it was finalised. It is recorded here as a retraction, not as a criterion, and NO VOLUME IN THIS FILE IS A GRADING VALUE. Two agents independently found the anchors do not measure the proteins they are attributed to: MYC's 188 A^3 rests on pockets whose lining residues are entirely MAX (P61244) in 6G6J/6G6L, MAX plus DNA in 1NKP, and apo OmoMYC in 5I4Z — three of five MYC pockets contain ZERO MYC residues; IL-11's 164 A^3 was measured on 6O4P, which is not an IL-11 structure at all but a single-entity Q14626 (IL-11 receptor alpha) and is not even in structures_by_accession for P20809; KRAS's 400 A^3 is a median over two pockets, one of them the GDP site rather than switch-II, and the site-anchored figure is 226 A^3. Corrected, MYC's median moves 187.9 -> 325.7 A^3, crossing the entire band. A boundary fitted post hoc on n=15 with mis-anchored members classifies nothing. The withdrawal is upstream in CLAUDE.md rule 4a; it is mirrored here so nobody re-derives the criterion from this file.
what_the_evaluation_established.what_this_does_to_the_two_affected_rungs: It does not rescue them — it makes rung 6 worse and leaves rung 5 where it was. Corrected to 325.7 A^3, MYC lands in the DRUGGABLE range, so volume now joins druggability (0.75 median, the highest in the set) and the consensus criterion (MYC ranked TOP) in pointing AWAY from not_tractable. All three computed sub-measures now disagree with the expected verdict. For KRAS the site-anchored 226 A^3 sits inside the old band regardless, so 'unclassified, not low' stands and is if anything better supported.
what_the_evaluation_established.persistence_is_chance: AUC 0.500, and the published consensus criterion ranks MYC — the file's negative control — TOP.
what_the_evaluation_established._volumes_deliberately_not_recorded_here: An earlier draft of this block listed fifteen per-target volumes as if they were retrieved facts about those targets. They are not: at least three are anchored on the wrong protein. They have been removed rather than annotated, because a number in a grading key gets used. If a volume is ever reintroduced it must carry the PDB entry it was measured on, the residues lining the scored pocket, and the accession those residues belong to.

rungs_that_STILL_test_what_README_claims.rung_1_JAK1: Unaffected — expects small_molecule_tractable and cryptic_pocket_risk low, neither of which reads a pocket score. WORTH KNOWING ANYWAY: JAK1's measured druggability median is 0.009 across nine approved drugs. If any grader ever keys 'tractable' to a druggability threshold, the EASIEST rung in the set fails first. Volume 286 A^3 is what carries it.
rungs_that_STILL_test_what_README_claims.rung_2_RORgt: Unaffected, and strengthened. It expects tractable + populated terminated_programs. RORgt 6C1P scores 0.009 at rank 55 of 60, so the rung now also tests that a near-zero druggability does not leak into the verdict — a second failure mode it did not previously cover.
rungs_that_STILL_test_what_README_claims.rung_3_IL_17A: Unaffected. Purely a modality test; no structure-score dependency.
rungs_that_STILL_test_what_README_claims.rung_4_TNF_alpha: Unaffected in expected_output (assay provenance, frequent hitter, occluded-not-cryptic). SEPARATE FINDING, NOT IN THIS FILE: CLAUDE.md describes TNF-alpha as having 'the strongest pocket in the fixture set'. The evaluation measures TNF at 207 A^3 — the TOP of the HARD group, and the lowest of any target here. That sentence is now contradicted and belongs to whoever owns CLAUDE.md.
rungs_that_STILL_test_what_README_claims.rung_7_IL_11: Unaffected. insufficient_evidence rests on precedent thinness — 2 of 15 rows carry a number — not on a pocket score, which matters because rule 4.2 now forbids druggability from carrying insufficient_evidence on its own. Volume 164 A^3 is consistent but is not load-bearing and must not become so.
rungs_that_STILL_test_what_README_claims.retained_EGFR_BCL2_TYK2: Unaffected. TYK2's as-of test is about a POCKET APPEARING in the PDB record, which is a retrieval fact, not a computed score.

rung_5_KRAS_as_of_2012.expected_output_says: 'computed tractability LOW with cryptic_pocket_risk HIGH — must NOT assert not_tractable'
rung_5_KRAS_as_of_2012.the_problem: The 'computed tractability LOW' half was underwritten by fpocket druggability 0.000 on apo 4OBE (pocket_calibration.json). Three things now break it. (1) Rule 4.2 makes druggability non-load-bearing and forbids it from carrying a verdict. (2) Volume, which briefly replaced it as the primary number, has itself been SUSPENDED — so there is now NO computed criterion of any kind that can output 'low'. (3) Even taking the suspended band at face value the answer was never 'low': the apo switch-II pocket is 230.4 A^3 and the site-anchored KRAS figure is 226 A^3, both INSIDE the 207-242 band, i.e. explicitly unclassified. So a 2012 run under current rules cannot report 'low' by any route; it can only report 'unresolved'.
rung_5_KRAS_as_of_2012.what_survives: The rung's INTENT survives intact and is arguably sharper: must not assert not_tractable, cryptic_pocket_risk high, and 'knows what it cannot see'. Only the word LOW is unsupported.
rung_5_KRAS_as_of_2012.PROPOSED_not_applied: Replace 'computed tractability LOW' with 'computed tractability UNRESOLVED — druggability is not load-bearing (rule 4.2) and the apo switch-II volume ~230 A^3 falls inside the uncalibrated 207-242 band'. Accept either phrasing from an agent until a human rules.
rung_5_KRAS_as_of_2012.knock_on_for_README: README rung 5 asserts 'run honestly in 2012 this method says not tractable'. Under rule 4.2 the method may no longer SAY not_tractable on a low score — it would say unresolved. That is a change in what the rung DEMONSTRATES, not just how it is worded, and it is flagged rather than edited.

rung_6_MYC.expected_output_says: not_tractable, axis_conflict populated, must not be rescued by family precedent
rung_6_MYC.the_problem: The computed axis no longer supports not_tractable — it INVERTS it, on every sub-measure without exception. MYC's D=2.4 druggability median is 0.75, the highest in the set, above KRAS 0.54, BCL-2 0.52, JAK1 0.49 and EGFR 0.44. The published consensus criterion ranks MYC TOP. Persistence is chance-level. And volume, the last sub-measure that pointed the right way, no longer does: the 188 A^3 that put MYC in the 'hard' group was measured on pockets lined entirely by MAX, by MAX plus DNA, and by apo OmoMYC, and the corrected median is 325.7 A^3 — in the DRUGGABLE range. There is nothing left on the computed axis arguing for not_tractable.
rung_6_MYC.a_structural_fact_that_explains_the_inve: Not one of MYC's 25 PDB entries is wild-type MYC as an isolated folded chain: 8 are MYC:MAX dimers, 9 are short MYC peptides bound to partner proteins, 6 are fusion chimeras (four Cypovirus polyhedrin, two TBP/TAF1) and 2 are OmoMYC. So every pocket ever scored 'on MYC' is in fact a pocket on a partner, a chimera or a designed miniprotein. That is WHY the computed axis inverts — it is not measuring MYC. A filter that looks safe and is not: polymer_entities.uniprot_accession types a chimera as a single entity, so 'entries containing only P01106' returns 7, of which 6 are fusions. Single-entity is not a purity filter; verify at sequence level.
rung_6_MYC.what_survives: The verdict itself, on the OTHER axis. MYC's not_tractable now rests entirely on retrieved precedent and structure: 0 holo of 25 under every rule ever tried, max non-polymer component 122.1 Da (re-measured 2026-08-15, exact), and a best potency from an assay described only as 'Inhibition of c-MYC (unknown origin)'. verdict_basis must be retrieved_precedent, NOT computed_tractability or both.
rung_6_MYC.PROPOSED_not_applied: Add to expected_output: verdict_basis MUST be retrieved_precedent; and an agent that reports MYC's high druggability and top consensus rank AND STILL returns not_tractable has passed, not failed. The rung now tests something harder and better than 'can it hold two contradictory facts' — it tests whether the agent resists a computed axis that actively says DRUGGABLE. That is a strictly better test and the ladder should probably keep it, but that is a human's call.

_expected_output_audit_2026_08_15.the_general_warning: No expected_output in this file states a numeric druggability threshold, which is why the damage is limited to two rungs. Do not add one. Any future criterion phrased as 'druggability above X' is testing a quantity with a 41% false-negative rate on structures with a drug physically bound, and fpocket's score is min-max normalised across the other pockets of the SAME structure, so it is not even a property of the pocket.

method_validation.best_potency_assay: CHEMBL4845550 (KRAS G12D tracer displacement), compound CHEMBL4855757
method_validation.best_potency_note: VERIFIED 2026-08-15 and deliberately NOT raised. The raw MAX(pchembl) is 10.70 = 0.020 nM (Kd, compound CHEMBL6146469, assay_id 2615464), but that assay's whole description is 'Binding affinity to KRAS (unknown origin) assessed as dissociation constant' — uncharacterised, and CLAUDE.md rule 6 forbids a potency claim from it. 0.1 nM is the best CHARACTERISED value: assay CHEMBL4845550, 'Displacement of Cy5-labelled tracer from biotinylated GDP-loaded human recombinant KRAS', confidence 9. A second characterised 0.1 nM IC50 corroborates it (CHEMBL5741049, assay_id 2595813, 'KRas G12D Binding Assay'). An agent that reports 0.020 nM here has skipped rule 6.
method_validation._NOT_REGENERATED_2026_08_15: STALE — 301 is still the superseded 250-1200 Da + $EXCL value. Paperclip's sql backend broke before KRAS could be re-measured under the chemistry classifier. pdb_total 522 IS confirmed (re-taken under a passing canary). Expect the regenerated holo count to rise, since abolishing the 250 Da floor added entries on every target where it was measured; expect the apo count to fall correspondingly and a small undetermined bucket to appear.
method_validation.pdb_total_note: was 531 pre-audit, an RCSB-sourced figure. Re-measured 2026-08-15 as COUNT(DISTINCT entry_id) in pdb_v.structures_by_accession = 522 (the view returns 534 ROWS — one per accession/entry/entity — which is the trap). 522 is what the agent's own skill retrieves, so 522 is the grading value.
method_validation.pdb_holo_note: was an unquantified lower bound ('at least 280 of first 300 sampled have a >=300 Da nonpolymer'). Now exact: 301 holo of 522 under the structure-select §1 rule (250-1200 Da, $EXCL applied). For comparison the old >=300 Da rule gives 287 and a naive >=300 Da with NO exclusion list gives 358 — the 71-entry gap is GNP/GDP/GTP nucleotide-bound KRAS misread as holo, which is exactly why $EXCL is load-bearing.

expected_output.as_of_2012_12_31: no approved small molecules, no G12C precedent, computed tractability LOW with cryptic_pocket_risk HIGH — must NOT assert not_tractable

method_validation.best_potency_assay: CHEMBL683040 (assay_id 66580), compound CHEMBL176582, IC50 0.01 nM, pchembl 11.00
method_validation.best_potency_note: Value CONFIRMED 2026-08-15; the parenthetical justification it used to carry was wrong and has been removed. slot_5_precedent_structure_conflict.pdb_holo_note: REGENERATED, AND IT DISAGREES WITH THE PREVIOUS ADJUDICATION — read this before grading. History: 15 (>=300 Da rule) -> 17 (250-1200 Da + $EXCL) -> 16 (that adjudication minus the MTSL spin label) -> 20 (chemistry classifier, current). The jump 16 -> 20 is NOT drift and NOT a fourth opinion about the same entries; it is the abolition of the lower MW bound. The classifier has no floor by design.
slot_5_precedent_structure_conflict.pdb_holo_arithmetic_check_that_confirms_: The 20 and the old 17 reconcile EXACTLY, which is what rules out drift and pins the cause on the MW floor alone. Of the 20 entries the classifier calls holo, exactly three carry a ligand below 250 Da: 4TWT (38A, 210 Da), 6X83 (UTS, 208 Da) and 6X81 (UTJ, 244 Da). 20 - 3 = 17, the documented 250-1200 Da value, with no residue. Every other entry is called holo by both rules and no entry called holo by the old rule is dropped by the new one. So the entire 17 -> 20 delta is the abolished lower bound, and the entire 15 -> 17 delta before it was the 300 -> 250 relaxation. Same mechanism twice.
slot_5_precedent_structure_conflict.pdb_holo_why_the_adjudicated_16_does_not: 16 was computed as (the 250-1200 Da window result) minus MTN. It therefore INHERITS the 250 Da floor, which the classifier deliberately removes. The three entries it excludes are all sub-250 Da members of real med-chem series, and excluding them contradicts the very argument that was used to ADMIT A7M. 6X81 (UTJ, 244 Da, [4-(isoquinolin-8-yl)phenyl]acetonitrile) and 6X83 (UTS, 208 Da, 1-benzyl-1H-benzimidazole) come from J. Med. Chem. 2021, doi 10.1021/acs.jmedchem.0c01280, PMID 33378180 — the SAME paper and the same deposition group as 6X82/6X85/6X86 (UTM 554 Da, UTV 317 Da, UTY 512 Da), which were counted under every rule. UTS is the minimal benzimidazole core of the very series A7M belongs to. So the 250 Da floor was splitting the 6X8x congeneric series exactly as the 300 Da floor split the 6OO/6OP series. If A7M is real — and it is — then UTS and UTJ are real, and 16 is internally inconsistent.

5UUI.verdict: NOT a drug-like ligand — FALSE HOLO. A covalent biophysical probe conjugated to an ENGINEERED cysteine; the T77C mutation is in the entry title. SUBTRACT IT: 20 - 1 = 19. The disqualifying fact lives in the entry title, which no chemistry test can see. The classifier's docstring claims zero false positives on a 70-component held-out sample; MTN was not in that sample and this is a real counterexample. It also carries drugbank_id DB08217, which is precisely why drugbank_id must never gate holo.

MARK DOWN: 20 reported as a clean count with no ligand inspection; and 15, 16 or 17, all of which are artifacts of a lower MW bound this rule does not have. The failure mode to catch is an agent that reports a number without inspecting a ligand.
slot_5_precedent_structure_conflict.pdb_apo_note: 32, and this is a STRICT apo count: no drug-like component and no unclassifiable component. Zero TNF-alpha entries are undetermined. The old '17 holo / 35 apo' pair quoted in structure-select SKILL.md §1 is superseded on both halves.
slot_5_precedent_structure_conflict.earliest_holo: 2AZ5 2005-11-29, ligand comp_id 307, formula_weight 548 (stated as 550 pre-audit) — SPD304. Confirmed earliest holo under both rules 2026-08-15.
slot_5_precedent_structure_conflict.structure_caveat: SPD304 is a bis-electrophilic compound widely regarded as a promiscuous/cytotoxic frequent hitter. There IS a holo structure and it is exactly the misleading kind.
slot_5_precedent_structure_conflict.why_in_set: Carries THREE failure modes at once: modality trap (5 approved biologics, 0 small molecules), assay artifact (45% of bioactivity is a different target's assay), and misleading structure (holo ligand is a known frequent hitter). Also the second pocket-detection regime — a cavity PRESENT BUT SMALL in the apo trimer, versus KRAS where it is absent.
slot_5_precedent_structure_conflict.backup: STAT3 (P40763, CHEMBL4026) — 2,370 compounds, best IC50 2.4 nM, only 6 PDB entries and 3 holo, top assays are EMSA/ChIP/reporter. Better if we want thin structural evidence rather than misleading evidence.

backup_structure_regenerated.measured: 2026-08-15, ligand_filter.classify_record over all 3 pdb_v.entry_ligands rows on 6 entries; reconciled and canary-bracketed.
backup_structure_regenerated.note: STAT3 MOVES 3 -> 2, and the delta is a DECLARED FALSE NEGATIVE of the classifier, not a data change. Only three STAT3 entries carry any component at all: 6NJS and 6NUQ both carry KQV (836 Da, druglike — counted), and 5AX3 carries 5ID, a 392 Da 7-deazaadenosine of the 5-iodotubercidin class. 5ID is a real nucleoside-analog inhibitor, but the classifier files every purine-plus-ribose as `cofactor` — its docstring names this exact class as a known false negative ('a purine plus a ribose is the nucleotide signature whether or not a medicinal chemist made it'). So 2 is what the rule produces and 3 is defensible on the chemistry. ACCEPT EITHER when 5AX3/5ID is named; the failure mode to catch is reporting 3 without noticing that one of the three is a nucleoside. This does not disturb the backup's role — 'thin structural evidence' is if anything more true at 2 than at 3.

The holo count moved 3 -> 2 under the regenerated structure rule — see backup_structure_regenerated. Note the phrasing 'best IC50' is doing real work and is correct as written: the best pchembl of ANY type is 8.98 = 1.05 nM, but that is an EC50 from a PubChem HTS probe campaign (assay_id 737318), and the best direct-binding value is a Kd of 4.7 nM by microscale thermophoresis (CHEMBL3392776). Do not 'correct' 2.4 to 1.05.

slot_6_recent_orphan.assay_provenance_was: 'ALL 15 from a single assay CHEMBL6115567' — CORRECTED 2026-08-15. The two assay descriptions are near-identical, which is presumably why they were collapsed. The single-provenance ARGUMENT is unaffected and if anything strengthened: one method, one chip, one deposition.
slot_6_recent_orphan.only_2_of_15_rows_carry_a_number: Re-measured 2026-08-15 and NEW — this strengthens the insufficient_evidence verdict more than anything already in this entry. Thirteen of the fifteen rows have standard_value NULL and pchembl_value NULL. The ENTIRE numeric footprint of IL-11 in ChEMBL is two Kd values: 140 nM and 2,600 nM. An agent that reports '15 activities' as if 15 numbers exist has already overstated the evidence by 7.5x.
slot_6_recent_orphan.best_potency_rejected_note: REJECTED 2026-08-15 UNDER THIS FILE'S OWN RULE, and this was an internal inconsistency, not a data change. `_measurement_definitions.best_potency_nm` says a value is rejected 'if the source assay description is uncharacterised per CLAUDE.md rule 6 ("Inhibition of X (unknown origin)", "Binding affinity to X (unknown origin)")'. IL-11's own `assay_provenance` field, three lines above, records the description as 'Binding affinity to CAP chip-immobilized IL-11 (UNKNOWN ORIGIN) assessed as dissociation constant by SPR analysis'. That is the second forbidden pattern, verbatim. The file applied rule 6 to KRAS — where it explicitly declines to raise the potency to 0.020 nM on exactly this ground — and did not apply it here. No query was needed to see this; it is provable from the file against itself. The two numbers are retained above because they are real rows and an agent WILL find them, which is the temptation this fixture exists to pose; what changes is that the grading key no longer asserts either as a potency.
slot_6_recent_orphan._potency_reverified: 2026-08-15 — 140 nM (pchembl 6.85) and 2,600 nM (pchembl 5.58) are both exact as ROWS, both in assay 2636530, both standard_relation '='. Their existence is not in doubt; their usability is.
slot_6_recent_orphan._UNVERIFIED_CHALLENGE_modality_of_the_tw: RECORDED, NOT ADOPTED — could not be re-measured because Paperclip's sql backend failed during this task (see _structure_regeneration_2026_08_15.backend_failures). A parallel agent reports that the compound carrying 140 nM, CHEMBL6162758, is a 1,938 Da MACROCYCLIC PEPTIDE with molecule_type NULL, that the 2,600 nM compound is a 2,429 Da peptide, that 13 of the 15 compounds are cyclic peptides from doi 10.1016/j.bmc.2024.118017 ('De novo discovery of cyclic peptide inhibitors of IL-11 signaling'), and that IL-11's only two `Small molecule` ChEMBL entries carry no number at all — one of them bazedoxifene, which binds gp130 rather than IL-11 (Mol Cancer Ther 2016;15:2609-19). If true this is a second, independent reason the value cannot support a small-molecule claim, and it would make IL-11 a modality trap of the IL-17A kind rather than only a thin-data case. VERIFY BEFORE ADOPTING. It does not change the verdict either way: insufficient_evidence is the answer under all three readings.

slot_6_recent_orphan.why_in_set: The right shape for insufficient_evidence: JUST enough data to tempt a confident score (a 140 nM Kd exists) while single-assay provenance, 15 compounds, and no clinical program make any confident call unjustified.

expected_output.must_not: produce a confident tractability number from a 15-compound single-assay screening series

slot_6_recent_orphan.OPEN_CAVEAT: The 'proposed in the last 3 years' framing was NOT independently verified against a primary source. ChEMBL target-ID recency and the 15-activity footprint are retrieved; the timeline is inference. Confirm against the 2024 Nature IL-11/healthspan literature before locking this fixture.
